response.rationale: The patient has confirmed dengue virus infection with evidence of plasma leakage (pleural effusions, pulmonary edema) and thrombocytopenia, supporting dengue hemorrhagic fever over uncomplicated dengue fever.

rejected.why: Elevated troponin and ECG changes are non-specific and can occur in the setting of critical illness or myocarditis; no evidence of obstructive coronary disease.
ARDS is a complication of the underlying infection, not the primary diagnosis; the clinical picture is best explained by severe dengue.
Normal thyroid function and lack of other features make thyroid storm unlikely.
Pulmonary edema is a manifestation of the underlying dengue-related capillary leak, not the primary diagnosis.
